## PM triage — `pm:blocked` on PR objectstack-ai/objectui#7146 landing

Gated on file collision: the funnel arm lives in `AdvancedChartImpl.tsx`, which PR objectui#7146 is editing and which has **not yet landed**. Unblocks automatically when it does.

### This card corrects a framing I had accepted

objectui#7140's body claimed the sankey was *"the last path that renders a blank tile and says nothing."* I carried that into objectui#7140's dispatch as an assumption to verify rather than a fact — and it came back **false**, in a way that matters more than a miscount:

The five blank tiles hash **identically** (`b53cc8c4…`), but they are two different defects. The sankey's blank is an **empty DOM** — one element, no `svg`, an early return. Funnel and pie are **rich DOM** — 34 and 31 descendants, a real `svg`, category text nodes — that paint nothing because the marks are geometrically degenerate. Zero area is not zero elements.

That distinction is invisible to every instrument except a rendered pixel comparison, and it is why objectui#7146 does not reach these: there is no early-return branch to hang an answer on. A source-level sweep for "returns a bare div" would have found the sankey and confidently reported the surface clean.

Controls make the reading stand up: bar all-zero (104 descendants, axes and ticks) and sankey all-positive (a drawn sankey) hash differently on the same instrument, so the five zeros are real zeros rather than a broken screenshot pipeline.

### Carried forward

The treemap observation folded into this card — all-zero rows painting ONE full-bleed leaf labelled with the LAST category — is a third shape again: not blank, but not an honest picture of two equal-zero categories. Worth measuring in the same pass rather than as a fourth card.

`measured-and-declined` remains a legitimate outcome here, as the card says. Render it and look at it first.

## 🔓 Unblocked — `pm:blocked` → `pm:queue`

PR objectstack-ai/objectui#7146 landed as `0349555c7`; the `AdvancedChartImpl.tsx` collision has cleared. Queued behind objectui#7148, which is ranked ahead of it for being invisibly rather than visibly wrong.

Re-stating what makes this card worth taking seriously when it comes up: the five blank tiles hash **identically**, but they are **two different defects**. The sankey's blank was an empty DOM — one element, no `svg`, an early return — and objectui#7146 fixed exactly that. Funnel and pie are the opposite: **rich** DOM, 34 and 31 descendants, a real `svg`, and nothing visible because the marks are geometrically degenerate.

**Zero area is not zero elements.** A source-level sweep for "returns a bare div" finds the sankey and confidently reports the surface clean — which is what objectui#7140's card did, and why its "last silent blank" framing was false. Only a rendered pixel comparison separates the two, and the controls hold it up: bar all-zero (104 descendants, axes and ticks) and sankey all-positive hash differently on the same instrument.

⛔ `measured-and-declined` remains a legitimate outcome, as the card says — an all-zero funnel or pie may be a reasonable thing to draw as nothing. **Render it and look at it first.** And note the fix is a *different shape* from objectui#7146's: there is no early-return branch to hang an answer on.

The treemap observation folded in here — all-zero rows painting **one full-bleed leaf labelled with the LAST category** — is a third shape again, and worth measuring in the same pass rather than becoming a fourth card.

## ⏸️ Re-blocked — `pm:queue` → `pm:blocked`, on a *different* PR than before

Correcting my own scheduling: I unblocked this an hour ago when PR objectui#7146 landed, then dispatched objectui#7148 into **`AdvancedChartImpl.tsx`** — the same file this card's funnel arm lives in. Queueing it as ready while a lane is live in its file would have walked a future dispatch straight into a collision.

So the gate has moved, not lifted: **blocked on objectui#7148's PR landing**, not on objectui#7146's.

Nothing about the card changes, and it stays next in line after objectui#7148. Restating the part that makes it worth taking:

The five blank tiles hash identically but are **two different defects**. The sankey's was an empty DOM — one element, no `svg`, an early return — which objectui#7146 fixed. Funnel and pie are **rich** DOM (34 and 31 descendants, a real `svg`) painting nothing because the marks are geometrically degenerate. **Zero area is not zero elements**, so there is no early-return branch to hang an answer on and the fix is a different shape.

⛔ `measured-and-declined` remains legitimate — render it and look first. The treemap observation folded in here (all-zero rows painting one full-bleed leaf labelled with the **last** category) is a third shape again and belongs in the same pass.

## 📎 Scope widened by measurement from objectui#7148 — this card is bigger than all-zero datasets

objectui#7148's implementer measured this while sweeping 27 tiles and, per my report-don't-fix fence, **did not file a duplicate card** — they reported it for attachment here. Correct call; recording it so it is not lost.

### The reader-facing symptom reaches these families on MIXED datasets too, not just all-zero ones

Measured with per-family all-positive controls in the same sweep:

| family | dataset | drew | control drew |
|---|---|---|---|
| treemap | mixed-sign | **2** rects / 2 labels | 4 / 4 |
| funnel | positive + `null` | **0** segment paths / 1 label | 2 / 2 |
| pie | positive + `null` | **1** slice | 2 |

So this card's population is **not** "all-zero rows produce a blank tile." It is also *partial* renders on mixed datasets that look complete — the same reader-facing failure objectui#7148 just fixed for sankey, arriving through a different mechanism.

### And the mechanism difference is why objectui#7148's fix cannot be hoisted here

Those rows are **never filtered**. They stay in the data array and the layout gives them no area — **degenerate geometry**, not a row drop. objectui#7148's footnote counts dropped rows (`data.length` vs `rows.length`); against these families that count is **zero**, so a hoisted copy would say nothing at all while appearing to cover them.

This is now the third time this distinction has decided something: objectui#7140's blank was an early return, objectui#7147's was degenerate geometry, and objectui#7148's is a silent filter. **Zero area is not zero elements, and neither is a dropped row.** Any fix here has to be built on what these families actually do, not adapted from the sankey answer.

Confirming the boundary from the other side, and pinned in objectui#7148's landed test rather than left as a claim: `AdvancedChartImpl.tsx:1047` is the **only** row-dropping filter in the entire file — the other two `.filter(` sites filter *series*, not rows. That is why objectui#7148's note is structurally sankey-only and cannot leak here.

### Still `pm:blocked`, gate unchanged

Blocked on PR objectstack-ai/objectui#7161 (objectui#7148) landing, since it is live in `AdvancedChartImpl.tsx`. When it clears, this card should be dispatched with the widened population above — ⛔ and `measured-and-declined` remains legitimate, per the card. Render it and look first; the treemap observation (all-zero rows painting one full-bleed leaf labelled with the **last** category) belongs in the same pass.

## ✅ LANDED — PR #7169 squash-merged to `main` (`5eddeeb68`)

Verified **by content with live controls**, never by sha. The strongest available shape here is differential — the two landed sibling answers are still in the same file, so they discriminate a real landing from a broken probe:

| probe | result |
|---|---|
| SUBJECT — `no-positive-magnitude` (this PR's refusal code) | **1** |
| SUBJECT — `unsized-rows` (this PR's note attribute) | **1** |
| SUBJECT — `countSizableRows` (the shared predicate) | **7** |
| SUBJECT — new suite `AdvancedChartImpl.degenerateMagnitude.test.tsx` present | **1** (control: 33 pre-existing suites in the same listing) |
| CONTROL — `no-positive-flow`, landed #7146 | **3** — still live |
| CONTROL — `omitted-rows`, landed #7161 | **1** — still live |

All four seam codes now coexist in `AdvancedChartImpl.tsx`, which is what the PR's mutual-exclusivity test asserts across every family × dataset pair.

## ⭐ The sweep is the result, and it is worse than the card claimed

74 tiles in real Chromium, screenshotted, MD5'd and pixel-diffed against an empty `div` of the same box. What a reader was actually getting:

- **pie / donut** on all-zero, all-null, all-negative: **0 non-white pixels of 124,800** — byte-identical to an empty `div`, while the DOM carried 31 descendants and a real `svg`.
- **pie** on `40` beside a `null`: a **full circle** in the first category's colour, **99.35% pixel-identical** to a legitimately one-row dataset. The picture asserts "Alpha is 100%" of a dataset where Beta was never measured.
- **funnel** on `40` beside a `null`: 178 ink pixels — **zero segments, one label, and the label reads "Beta"**, the row with no value. The row carrying 40 drew nothing.
- **funnel** on all-negative: a confident two-band funnel whose mark area (220,320) *exceeds* the all-positive control's (111,881).
- **treemap**: `40/null`, `40/0`, `40/-25/-12` all **byte-identical** (diff `0.000%`) to a one-row treemap. **Four datasets, one image.**

## The three things that make this a measurement rather than a fix

**1. `measured-and-declined` survived for bar and radar.** An all-zero **bar** puts 5,128 ink pixels of axes and ticks against a blank tile's 0 — its reader can already tell. Declining part of the population on evidence is a first-class result, and it is what makes the other six verdicts credible.

**2. #7148's footnote could NOT be hoisted, and that was confirmed rather than assumed.** The rows here are **never filtered** — `data` reaches the elements whole; the layout simply gives a non-positive row no area. So #7161's count (`data.length - rows.length`) is **exactly zero** against these families. ⭐ A hoisted copy would have rendered nothing while looking like coverage. Verified by the sweep: the sankey tiles are the only ones carrying `omitted-rows`.

**3. A2.3 was falsified in one respect and it changed nothing.** Pie and funnel are *not* the same failure at the Recharts level — an unsizable pie row produces **no sector element at all**, an unsizable funnel row produces a **NaN-width trapezoid that poisons its neighbour** (which is why `40` beside a `null` loses the row worth 40, not the null one), and a treemap leaf collapses while its neighbours expand. **Three Recharts behaviours, one authoring-side predicate** — `Number.isFinite(v) && v > 0`, chosen over the sankey arm's `Number(x) || 0` because it must also reject `Infinity`, which `|| 0` passes straight through.

The note deliberately does **not** say "showing N of M": a mixed-sign pie *paints* a sector for every row (measured: `40/-25/-12` drew 3), so that sentence would be false about what is on screen.

## Evidence quality

Two ablation legs, direction predicted before running, with **disjoint red sets** — refusal-guard neutered gave `26 failed / 38 passed` all in the refusal block; note-guard neutered gave `26 failed / 38 passed` all in the note block. Each left the other 38 green, which is what makes them discriminating rather than a blanket break. And the "before" column is the real thing: the pre-fix renderer was reproduced by double ablation and **verified 56/56 tiles byte-identical** against the true pre-fix run. **24 tiles changed, 50 did not** — including all 9 bar and all 9 sankey tiles byte-identical, so both landed answers keep firing under their own codes.

The console-diagnostic zero across 72 tiles is readable **only** because the same instrument's positive control fired on the same run. A control that returns zero is no control.

## ⚠️ Two things this card leaves behind

**#7171 — scatter is NOT MEASURED, not clean.** Its all-positive control drew **zero marks** on this instrument, so its zeros say nothing; scatter takes two measures and the sweep's single-measure fixture does not bind it. The implementer correctly declined to file it under the report-don't-duplicate fence and handed it back; I filed it. **Now unblocked to `pm:queue`.**

**The footnote-visibility note carries forward, and it is not this PR's defect.** A 520×240 tile — the box the card's own sweep used — is **40px shorter than `CHART_MIN_HEIGHT` (280)**, so no footnote can be seen in it. Measured with #7161's *landed* note as the control: `sankey--posNull` is byte-identical before and after at 240, i.e. **the already-shipped note is equally invisible there**. A pre-existing property of sub-280 boxes, inherited and not worsened.

Clearing `pm:dispatched`.
